Run every rule in a registry, one at a time

Source: R/qc.R
qc_run_all.Rd

Sequential on purpose: these are multi-GB scans and running them concurrently against one DuckDB just contends for the same buffer pool.

Usage

qc_run_all(
  con,
  rules,
  limit = 500L,
  on_progress = NULL,
  present_types = qc_present_types(con),
  scope_values = list()
)

Arguments

con

a DBI connection carrying the tables the rule targets

rules

a rule registry from qc_read_rules()

limit

cap on rows returned. The COUNT is always computed over the full result, so a truncated display never understates the problem — a rule that silently showed 500 of 40,000 hits would read as "minor".

on_progress

optional function(i, n, rule_key) callback

present_types

output of qc_present_types(); NULL disables the check

scope_values

named list supplying scope parameters, e.g. list(cruise_key = "2023-11-33P4"). A rule with scope = "cruise" reads the full-resolution obs_ctd_full and is meaningless unscoped, so it SKIPS rather than silently scanning everything.

Value

list of qc_run_rule() results, in registry order
